cases.question: How accurate has this forecast actually been?
cases.answer: Our live track record shows an overall mean absolute error (MAE) of 9.2 across 5,868 scored points, beating CAMS in 80 of 83 days with an overall skill score of 51.6% against CAMS and 41.5% against persistence. cases.question: Is this better than the Copernicus CAMS forecast?
cases.answer: Yes, this system beats the Copernicus CAMS forecast overall, achieving a skill score of 51.6% against CAMS with an overall mean absolute error (MAE) of 9.2 compared to CAMS' 19.0. In fact, it has beaten CAMS on 80 of 83 days evaluated.

cases.question: How good is the 1-hour forecast?
cases.answer: For the live 1–6 hour bucket, the live track record shows an MAE of 6.759 with a skill of 68.6% vs CAMS and 27.0% vs persistence. In the backtest at the 1-hour lead time specifically, the MAE is 2.817 with an R² of 0.946, 73.9% skill vs CAMS, and an 80% range coverage of 83.1%.

cases.question: What drives the forecast the most?
cases.answer: The top driver behind the 24-hour forecast is "Measured minus CAMS (now)" (`cams_gap`), with a mean SHAP value of 6.68. This is followed by the "CAMS forecast for target hour" (`fut_cams_pm25`) at 4.04, and "Forecast wind speed" (`fut_wind_speed`) at 3.13.

cases.question: Why does the model use CAMS as an input if CAMS is wrong?
cases.answer: Even though CAMS can be inaccurate on its own, the model uses it as an informative input feature (achieving a live skill score of 0.516 versus CAMS and beating it on 80 of 83 days). By combining CAMS with local ground observations and other drivers, our machine learning model corrects CAMS's errors and achieves a much lower MAE (overall MAE of 9.212 versus CAMS MAE of 19.034).
